correctness.rationale: For an outcome path hitting +m, the diagonal product is (pq)^{N_-/2}diag(q^{m/2},p^{m/2}); all such products are positive scalar multiples, giving Kraus rank one for the whole stopped + completely positive map. Gambler-ruin hitting probabilities produce diagonal effect (q^m,p^m)/(q^m+p^m), giving W_+=diag(sqrt(1-p_m),sqrt(p_m)); reflection gives W_-. Therefore off-diagonal channel multiplier is 2sqrt(p_m(1-p_m)), maximal trace-distance dephasing disturbance (1-2sqrt(p_m(1-p_m)))/2, saturating the same source one-shot bounds. Optional stopping on bounded-interval walk gives E tau=m(1-2p_m)/(q-p). Own exact rational recurrence checks at p=1/4 with m=2,4 and p=2/5 with m=3 confirm the equations, but symbolic path-factor and ruin derivations cover all allowed parameters.

value.rationale: A sharp information–disturbance equality family generally need not remain extremal under adaptive repetition and record erasure. Here exact sign-conditioned Kraus rank one shows it does, with an explicit error-versus-measurement-count tradeoff. This is a motivated quantitative benchmark for ideal repeated QND readout, not just an information-theory reparameterization.

final_claim: For 0<p<1/2 repeated diagonal QND qubit Kraus operators diag(sqrt(1-p),sqrt(p)) and its reversed partner, first-hitting stopping at score ±m (m>=1) followed by sign-only coarse-graining is exactly the original two-outcome extremal instrument at p_m=p^m/(p^m+(1-p)^m); it saturates the original sharp decoherence/information-disturbance frontier with expected duration m((1-p)^m-p^m)/((1-2p)((1-p)^m+p^m)).
limitations: Only the ideal symmetric diagonal nondestructive qubit instrument with two score increments and finite ±m boundaries.
No optimal stopping time among all quantum instruments is established.
